patterns_found.visual_evidence: The mobile sketch shows a simplified top header with branding and no visible full navigation list, implying a collapsed mobile navigation control rather than persistent links.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: A tap target should open and close a mobile navigation panel or drawer containing the site links. The current page should be indicated within that menu.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not explicitly draw the hamburger icon or the opened drawer state, so the exact menu presentation (overlay, slide-in drawer, dropdown) is inferred from the mobile header simplification.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches place a narrow header/navigation strip at the very top above a long scrolling page with substantial content below, suggesting the header may remain available during scroll.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: If implemented as implied, the top navigation/header should remain fixed or become fixed after scrolling so branding/navigation stays accessible on long pages.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketches do not explicitly show repeated header states during scroll, so this may also be a static header rather than a sticky one.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The inferred mobile collapsed navigation implies an off-canvas or overlay menu that would require keyboard focus to move into the opened menu and return to the trigger when closed.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: When the mobile menu opens, focus should move to the menu or first actionable item; closing should restore focus to the trigger. Background interaction should be managed appropriately.
patterns_found.ambiguities: This depends on the mobile navigation being implemented as an overlay/drawer rather than a simple inline expansion.

sketch_notes: These sketches imply a mostly content-driven marketing page with minimal JavaScript needs. The clearest cross-viewport difference is navigation: desktop appears to expose links directly in the header, while mobile likely collapses navigation into a menu trigger. No forms, tabs, accordions, modals, search, or dynamic loading controls are visibly suggested. Any sticky behavior is only weakly implied by the long-scroll layout and top header placement.
